stem: How many neutrons are in a <sup>35</sup>Cl<sup>−</sup> ion?
explanation: Z = 17, so neutrons = 35 − 17 = 18. The extra electron does not change the nucleus.

stem: Which element has the largest atomic radius?
explanation: Radius shrinks across a period as nuclear charge rises, so Na, at the far left, is largest.

stem: Which molecule is polar?
explanation: NH<sub>3</sub> is trigonal pyramidal with a lone pair, so its bond dipoles do not cancel. The others are symmetric.

stem: A gas at 1.0 atm occupies 2.0 L. At constant temperature it is compressed to 0.50 L. What is the new pressure?
explanation: Boyle’s law: P<sub>2</sub> = P<sub>1</sub>V<sub>1</sub>/V<sub>2</sub> = (1.0)(2.0)/0.50 = 4.0 atm.

stem: How many moles of oxygen atoms are in 0.50 mol of Al<sub>2</sub>(SO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>?
explanation: Each formula unit has 3 × 4 = 12 O atoms, so 0.50 × 12 = 6.0 mol.

stem: In 2H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2H<sub>2</sub>O, 3.0 g H<sub>2</sub> reacts with 32 g O<sub>2</sub>. What mass of water forms? (H = 1.0, O = 16)
explanation: H<sub>2</sub> is 1.5 mol; 1.0 mol O<sub>2</sub> would need 2.0 mol H<sub>2</sub>, so H<sub>2</sub> limits. 1.5 mol × 18 g/mol = 27 g.

stem: What is the oxidation number of Cr in K<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub>?
Given C + O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub>, ΔH = −394 kJ, and CO + ½O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub>, ΔH = −283 kJ, find ΔH for C + ½O<sub>2</sub> → CO.
explanation: Subtract the second equation from the first: −394 − (−283) = −111 kJ.

stem: N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2NH<sub>3</sub> is exothermic. What happens to K when the temperature rises?
explanation: Heat acts like a product, so a higher temperature favors reactants and lowers K. Only temperature changes K.

stem: A first-order reaction has a half-life of 20 min. What fraction of the reactant remains after 60 min?
explanation: 60 min is three half-lives, so (1/2)<sup>3</sup> = 1/8.

stem: What volume of 0.125 M NaOH neutralizes 25.0 mL of 0.100 M HCl?
What is the pH of 0.0010 M Ba(OH)<sub>2</sub> at 25 °C?
A spot travels 3.0 cm while the solvent front travels 6.0 cm. What is its R<sub>f</sub>?
explanation: R<sub>f</sub> = spot distance ÷ solvent front distance = 3.0 ÷ 6.0 = 0.50.

stem: A buffer is 0.10 M CH<sub>3</sub>COOH and 0.20 M CH<sub>3</sub>COONa (pK<sub>a</sub> = 4.76). What is its pH?
explanation: Henderson–Hasselbalch: pH = 4.76 + log(0.20/0.10) = 4.76 + 0.30 = 5.06.

stem: The functional group in CH<sub>3</sub>COCH<sub>3</sub> is a…
explanation: A carbonyl bonded to two carbon atoms is a ketone (propanone).

stem: How many structural isomers does C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>12</sub> have?
explanation: Pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane.

stem: CH<sub>2</sub>=CH<sub>2</sub> + Br<sub>2</sub> → CH<sub>2</sub>BrCH<sub>2</sub>Br is which type of reaction?
explanation: Br<sub>2</sub> adds across the C=C double bond, so this is an addition reaction.

stem: A peptide bond forms between…
choices: the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another, releasing water
the R groups of two amino acids
explanation: It is a condensation reaction: −COOH + H<sub>2</sub>N− → −CO−NH− + H<sub>2</sub>O.

stem: How many significant figures are in 0.003040?
explanation: Leading zeros do not count; the trailing zero after the decimal does. The digits 3, 0, 4, 0 give 4.

stem: The mean of 10.2, 10.4, 10.1 and 10.3 is…
Which change is a chemical change?
explanation: Rusting forms a new substance (iron oxide). The others change only the state or the mixing.

stem: A metal block has mass 54.0 g and volume 20.0 cm<sup>3</sup>. What is its density?
explanation: Density = mass ÷ volume = 54.0 ÷ 20.0 = 2.70 g/cm<sup>3</sup>.

stem: How many electrons are in a Fe<sup>3+</sup> ion? (Fe: Z = 26)
explanation: A neutral Fe atom has 26 electrons; a 3+ ion has lost 3, leaving 23.

stem: A compound is 40.0% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O by mass. What is its empirical formula?
explanation: Per 100 g: C 3.33 mol, H 6.65 mol, O 3.33 mol. The ratio is 1 : 2 : 1.

stem: At 273 K and 1.00 atm, 5.60 L of a gas has a mass of 11.0 g. What is its molar mass? (molar volume = 22.4 L/mol)
Which phase change occurs when dry ice (solid CO<sub>2</sub>) is left at room pressure?
explanation: At 1 atm, CO<sub>2</sub> has no liquid phase, so the solid goes directly to gas: sublimation.

stem: Which set of quantum numbers (n, l, m<sub>l</sub>) is NOT allowed?
explanation: l can only run from 0 to n − 1, so l = 2 is impossible when n = 2.

stem: Boron’s first ionization energy is lower than beryllium’s mainly because…
choices: B has a larger nuclear charge
the 2p electron removed from B is higher in energy and better shielded than the 2s electron removed from Be
B has two more electron shells
explanation: The 2p electron sits slightly farther out and is shielded by the 2s electrons, so it is easier to remove.

stem: Which compound has the largest lattice energy?
explanation: Lattice energy grows with ion charge and falls with ion size. MgO has 2+/2− charges and small ions.

stem: What is the molecular shape of SF<sub>4</sub>?
explanation: Five electron domains (four bonds, one lone pair) give a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement with a seesaw shape.

stem: Which compound has the highest boiling point?
explanation: H<sub>2</sub>O forms extensive hydrogen bonds, the strongest intermolecular force of the four.

stem: What is the freezing point of a solution of 0.50 mol glucose in 1.0 kg water? (K<sub>f</sub> = 1.86 °C·kg/mol)
explanation: ΔT<sub>f</sub> = K<sub>f</sub>m = 1.86 × 0.50 = 0.93 °C. Glucose does not ionize, so the freezing point is −0.93 °C.

stem: How much heat raises 200 g of water from 20.0 °C to 30.0 °C? (c = 4.18 J/g·°C)
A rate constant doubles when the temperature rises from 300 K to 310 K. What is E<sub>a</sub>? (R = 8.314 J/mol·K)
A reaction has ΔH = +40 kJ/mol and ΔS = +100 J/mol·K. Above what temperature is it spontaneous?
explanation: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS < 0 when T > 40 000 ÷ 100 = 400 K.

stem: At 298 K a reaction has ΔG° = −11.4 kJ/mol. What is K? (R = 8.314 J/mol·K)
For A ⇌ B, K<sub>c</sub> = 4.0. If [A] = 0.50 M and [B] = 3.0 M, the system…
explanation: Q = 3.0 ÷ 0.50 = 6.0, which is greater than K, so the reaction shifts left to lower Q.

stem: The K<sub>sp</sub> of AgCl is 1.8 × 10<sup>−10</sup>. What is its molar solubility in pure water?
explanation: K<sub>sp</sub> = s<sup>2</sup>, so s = √(1.8 × 10<sup>−10</sup>) = 1.3 × 10<sup>−5</sup> M.

stem: For Zn + Cu<sup>2+</sup> → Zn<sup>2+</sup> + Cu, E° (Cu<sup>2+</sup>/Cu) = +0.34 V and E° (Zn<sup>2+</sup>/Zn) = −0.76 V. What is E°<sub>cell</sub>?
explanation: E°<sub>cell</sub> = E°<sub>cathode</sub> − E°<sub>anode</sub> = 0.34 − (−0.76) = +1.10 V.

stem: A cell has Zn²⁺ at 0.010 M and Cu<sup>2+</sup> at 1.0 M, with E°<sub>cell</sub> = 1.10 V at 25 °C. What is E<sub>cell</sub>?
What is the coordination number of Co in [Co(en)<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub>]<sup>+</sup>? (en = ethylenediamine, bidentate)
explanation: Two bidentate en ligands give 4 donor atoms, plus 2 Cl, so 6.

stem: How many atoms belong to one face-centred cubic unit cell?
explanation: 8 corners × 1/8 + 6 faces × 1/2 = 4 atoms.

stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>?
explanation: The longest chain has 4 carbons (butane). Numbering from the end nearest the branch puts the methyl on C2.

stem: How many stereoisomers does 2,3-dibromopentane have?
explanation: It has two different stereocentres (C2 and C3) and no internal symmetry, so 2<sup>2</sup> = 4.

stem: Which pair reacts in a [4+2] cycloaddition (Diels–Alder) to give a cyclohexene?
explanation: A conjugated diene (4 π electrons) adds to an alkene (2 π electrons) to form a six-membered ring.

stem: A compound has a strong IR band near 1715 cm<sup>−1</sup> and no broad band near 3300 cm<sup>−1</sup>. It is most likely…
explanation: 1715 cm<sup>−1</sup> is a C=O stretch. A carboxylic acid would also show a broad O–H band, so this is a ketone.

stem: In the <sup>1</sup>H NMR spectrum of ethanol, the CH<sub>3</sub> signal appears as a…
explanation: The CH<sub>3</sub> protons are next to a CH<sub>2</sub> (2 protons), so n + 1 = 3 lines: a triplet.

stem: A 2.0 × 10<sup>−4</sup> M solution in a 1.00 cm cell has an absorbance of 0.50. What is its molar absorptivity?
A 50.0 mL water sample needs 12.5 mL of 0.0100 M EDTA to reach the endpoint. EDTA binds metal ions 1:1. What is the total metal ion concentration?
explanation: mol EDTA = 0.0125 × 0.0100 = 1.25 × 10<sup>−4</sup>; divided by 0.0500 L gives 2.50 × 10<sup>−3</sup> M.

stem: MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup> + 5Fe<sup>2+</sup> + 8H<sup>+</sup> → Mn<sup>2+</sup> + 5Fe<sup>3+</sup> + 4H<sub>2</sub>O. If 20.0 mL of 0.0200 M KMnO<sub>4</sub> titrates a Fe<sup>2+</sup> sample, how many moles of Fe<sup>2+</sup> were present?
explanation: mol MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup> = 4.00 × 10<sup>−4</sup>; the 1 : 5 ratio gives 2.00 × 10<sup>−3</sup> mol Fe<sup>2+</sup>.

stem: What is the density of NH<sub>3</sub> gas at 27 °C and 1.00 atm? (R = 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K; M = 17.03 g/mol)
A 10.0 L flask holds 2.00 mol He and 3.00 mol Ne at 300 K. What is the partial pressure of Ne? (R = 0.0821 L·atm/mol·K)
explanation: P<sub>total</sub> = nRT/V = (5.00)(0.0821)(300) ÷ 10.0 = 12.3 atm. Ne is 3/5 of the moles, so its partial pressure is 0.600 × 12.3 = 7.39 atm.

stem: How many times faster does H<sub>2</sub> effuse than O<sub>2</sub> at the same temperature?
explanation: Graham’s law: rate ∝ 1/√M. The ratio is √(32.0 ÷ 2.02) ≈ √16 = 4.

stem: On a phase diagram, the point where solid, liquid and gas coexist in equilibrium is the…
explanation: The triple point is the one temperature and pressure where all three phases coexist.

stem: A metal crystallizes in a body-centred cubic lattice. How many atoms are in the unit cell, and what is the coordination number?
explanation: Atoms per cell = 8 corners × 1/8 + 1 centre = 2. Each atom touches 8 neighbours. (Face-centred cubic would be 4 atoms and 12 neighbours.)

stem: What is the ground-state electron configuration of Fe<sup>2+</sup>? (Fe: Z = 26)
explanation: Neutral Fe is [Ar] 4s<sup>2</sup>3d<sup>6</sup>. Transition metals lose their 4s electrons first, so Fe<sup>2+</sup> is [Ar] 3d<sup>6</sup>.

stem: How many unpaired electrons does a ground-state nitrogen atom have?
explanation: N is 1s<sup>2</sup>2s<sup>2</sup>2p<sup>3</sup>. By Hund’s rule the three 2p electrons occupy separate orbitals with parallel spins, giving 3 unpaired electrons.

stem: What is the energy of one photon of wavelength 500 nm? (h = 6.626 × 10<sup>−34</sup> J·s; c = 3.00 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s)
Which of these atoms has the most negative electron affinity?
explanation: Cl releases the most energy on gaining an electron. F is slightly less negative because its small 2p subshell has strong electron–electron repulsion. Br is less negative than Cl, and Ne has no favourable electron affinity.

stem: Which compound has the highest melting point?
explanation: MgO has 2+/2− ions that are small, so its lattice energy is the largest and it melts at about 2850 °C.

stem: What is the hybridization of carbon in CO<sub>2</sub>?
explanation: Carbon has 2 electron domains (two double bonds), so the geometry is linear and the hybridization is sp.

stem: What is the formal charge on nitrogen in the nitrate ion, NO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup>?
explanation: Formal charge = valence electrons − nonbonding electrons − bonds = 5 − 0 − 4 = +1 (three N–O bonds, one of them double).

stem: Which species has bond angles closest to 109.5°?
explanation: NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> is a perfect tetrahedron (109.5°). BF<sub>3</sub> is 120°, CO<sub>2</sub> is 180° and H<sub>2</sub>O is about 104.5°.

stem: Which substance has the strongest London dispersion forces?
explanation: Dispersion forces grow with the size and polarizability of the electron cloud. C<sub>8</sub>H<sub>18</sub> is the largest molecule.

stem: What volume of 12.0 M HCl is needed to make 500 mL of 0.600 M HCl?
explanation: M<sub>1</sub>V<sub>1</sub> = M<sub>2</sub>V<sub>2</sub>, so V<sub>1</sub> = (0.600 × 500) ÷ 12.0 = 25.0 mL.

stem: Which 0.10 m aqueous solution has the lowest freezing point?
explanation: ΔT<sub>f</sub> = iK<sub>f</sub>m. CaCl<sub>2</sub> gives three ions (i ≈ 3), NaCl two, while glucose and the weak acid CH<sub>3</sub>COOH give about one. The largest i gives the lowest freezing point.

stem: ΔH<sub>f</sub>° is −393.5 kJ/mol for CO<sub>2</sub>(g), −285.8 kJ/mol for H<sub>2</sub>O(l) and −74.8 kJ/mol for CH<sub>4</sub>(g). What is ΔH° for CH<sub>4</sub> + 2O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O(l)?

5.00 g of NH<sub>4</sub>NO<sub>3</sub> (M = 80.04 g/mol) dissolves in 100.0 g of water in a coffee-cup calorimeter, and the temperature falls from 25.0 °C to 21.0 °C. Taking c = 4.18 J/g·°C for the 105.0 g solution, what is ΔH of dissolution per mole?
explanation: Heat absorbed = 105.0 × 4.18 × 4.0 = 1756 J. Moles = 5.00 ÷ 80.04 = 0.06247. ΔH = 1.756 kJ ÷ 0.06247 = +28.1 kJ/mol. It is positive because the process takes in heat (the temperature drops).

stem: For A + B → products, doubling [A] doubles the rate and doubling [B] quadruples it. What is the rate law?
explanation: 2<sup>1</sup> = 2 means first order in A. 2<sup>2</sup> = 4 means second order in B. So rate = k[A][B]<sup>2</sup>.

stem: A first-order reaction has k = 0.0231 min<sup>−1</sup>. How long does it take for 75% of the reactant to be used up?
explanation: 25% remains, so t = ln(1/0.25) ÷ k = 1.386 ÷ 0.0231 = 60.0 min. This is two half-lives of 30 min each.

stem: Which process has a negative ΔS?
explanation: The ammonia synthesis goes from 4 mol of gas to 2 mol, so disorder falls. Melting, evaporating and dissolving all increase entropy.

stem: H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2HI has K<sub>c</sub> = 50.0 at 700 K. At equilibrium [H<sub>2</sub>] = [I<sub>2</sub>] = 0.020 M. What is [HI]?
For N<sub>2</sub>(g) + 3H<sub>2</sub>(g) ⇌ 2NH<sub>3</sub>(g), which change shifts the equilibrium to the right?
choices: Increasing the volume of the container
explanation: Removing a product pulls the equilibrium toward products. A larger volume or lower pressure favours the side with more gas moles (the left), and a catalyst does not shift the equilibrium.

stem: A current of 2.00 A passes through molten NaCl for 965 s. What mass of sodium is deposited? (F = 96 485 C/mol; M of Na = 22.99 g/mol)
What is the pH of 0.100 M acetic acid? (K<sub>a</sub> = 1.8 × 10<sup>−5</sup>)
What is the pH of 0.020 M NaOH at 25 °C?
A solution has absorbance 0.300 in a 1.00 cm cell and a molar absorptivity of 1.50 × 10<sup>3</sup> L mol<sup>−1</sup> cm<sup>−1</sup>. What is its concentration?
Which compound is an aldehyde?
explanation: An aldehyde has the –CHO group at the end of the chain: CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CHO is propanal. The others are a ketone, a carboxylic acid and an ether.

stem: Heating a primary alcohol with excess acidified K<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> gives…
explanation: The alcohol is first oxidized to an aldehyde, and with excess oxidant it goes on to the carboxylic acid. Ketones come from secondary alcohols.

stem: What is the oxidation state of copper in [Cu(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>4</sub>]SO<sub>4</sub>?
explanation: Sulfate is 2−, so the complex ion is 2+. NH<sub>3</sub> is neutral, so copper must be +2.

stem: A spherical gold nanoparticle has a radius of 2.50 nm. Gold has a density of 19.3 g/cm<sup>3</sup> and a molar mass of 197.0 g/mol. How many gold atoms are in one nanoparticle?
The speed of light is 3.00 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s. Express this speed in furlongs per fortnight. (1 furlong = 201.168 m; 1 fortnight = 14 days)
explanation: 3.00 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s ÷ 201.168 m/furlong = 1.491 × 10<sup>6</sup> furlongs/s. A fortnight is 14 × 86 400 = 1.2096 × 10<sup>6</sup> s, so the speed is 1.80 × 10<sup>12</sup> furlongs/fortnight. (The source key listed 1.80 × 10<sup>14</sup>, which is off by a factor of 100.)

stem: Which of the following statements describes an intensive physical property?
choices: The total heat capacity of a sample of water is 418.4 J/K.
A sample of copper has a volume of 12.5 mL.
The standard boiling point of ethanol is 78.37 °C.
The mass of a gold bar is 1.00 kg.
explanation: Intensive properties do not depend on the amount of sample. The boiling point is the same for 1 mL or 1 L of ethanol, while heat capacity, volume and mass all scale with the amount.

stem: Evaluate (14.285 − 0.0821) × 0.05200 ÷ (3.14159 + 0.002) and give the answer to the appropriate number of significant figures.
explanation: Subtraction: 14.285 − 0.0821 = 14.203 (3 decimal places). Addition: 3.14159 + 0.002 = 3.144 (3 decimal places). Then 14.203 × 0.05200 ÷ 3.144 = 0.2349. Of the listed values, 0.235 is the closest; a strict four-significant-figure result would be 0.2349, which is not offered.

stem: A cylindrical cork (density 0.240 g/cm<sup>3</sup>, length 10.0 cm, cross-sectional area 1.50 cm<sup>2</sup>) floats vertically in a fluid of density 1.20 g/cm<sup>3</sup>. How much of its length is below the surface?
explanation: A floating object displaces fluid equal to its own weight, so the submerged fraction is 0.240 ÷ 1.20 = 0.200. Submerged length = 0.200 × 10.0 cm = 2.00 cm. The cross-sectional area cancels out.

stem: A container weighs 22.10 g empty, 45.50 g filled with water (0.998 g/mL at 20 °C) and 51.20 g filled with an unknown liquid at the same temperature. What is the density of the unknown liquid?
explanation: Water mass = 45.50 − 22.10 = 23.40 g, so the container volume is 23.40 ÷ 0.998 = 23.45 mL. Liquid mass = 51.20 − 22.10 = 29.10 g. Density = 29.10 ÷ 23.45 = 1.24 g/mL. (The source key listed 1.13 g/mL, which does not follow from the data.)

stem: Which of the following processes is a chemical change?
choices: Tarnishing of silver cutlery in air
explanation: Tarnishing converts silver into silver sulfide, a new substance. The other three change only the state or the mixing; the substances themselves stay the same.

stem: A new temperature scale, °X, is related to Celsius by °X = 1.50(°C) + 20.0. What is absolute zero (−273.15 °C) on the °X scale?
Homogeneous mixtures differ from pure substances because homogeneous mixtures:
choices: can be separated into simpler substances by physical methods.
have a fixed composition regardless of preparation.
consist of only one type of atom.
cannot exist in the gas phase.
explanation: A mixture can be split into its components by physical means such as distillation or filtration; a pure substance (element or compound) cannot. Fixed composition describes pure compounds, and air is a gaseous homogeneous mixture.

stem: A sheet of platinum foil measures 2.50 cm × 4.00 cm and has a mass of 1.076 g. The density of platinum is 21.45 g/cm<sup>3</sup>. What is the thickness of the foil in micrometers (µm)?
explanation: V = 1.076 ÷ 21.45 = 0.05016 cm<sup>3</sup>. Area = 2.50 × 4.00 = 10.0 cm<sup>2</sup>, so thickness = 0.005016 cm. Since 1 cm = 10<sup>4</sup> µm, this is 50.2 µm.

stem: Millikan found the charge of the electron to be −1.602 × 10<sup>−19</sup> C, and Thomson measured e/m = −1.76 × 10<sup>8</sup> C/g. What is the mass of one electron?
explanation: m = e ÷ (e/m) = 1.602 × 10<sup>−19</sup> C ÷ 1.76 × 10<sup>8</sup> C/g = 9.10 × 10<sup>−28</sup> g. The 10<sup>−31</sup> option is the same mass expressed in kg.

stem: A uranium-238 atom (Z = 92) emits one alpha particle, then two beta (β<sup>−</sup>) particles. What is the resulting nuclide?
explanation: Alpha emission lowers the mass number by 4 and Z by 2, giving <sup>234</sup>Th (Z = 90). Each beta emission raises Z by 1 with no change in mass number: <sup>234</sup>Pa, then <sup>234</sup>U (Z = 92).

stem: Chlorine has two stable isotopes: <sup>35</sup>Cl (34.9688 amu) and <sup>37</sup>Cl (36.9659 amu). The average atomic mass is 35.4527 amu. What is the percent abundance of <sup>37</sup>Cl?
How many protons, neutrons and electrons are in one <sup>59</sup>Ni<sup>3+</sup> ion? (Ni: Z = 28)
explanation: Protons = Z = 28. Neutrons = 59 − 28 = 31. A 3+ ion has lost three electrons: 28 − 3 = 25.

stem: Rutherford’s gold foil experiment showed that:
choices: electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed energy levels.
electrons are embedded in a uniform sphere of positive charge.
most of the mass and all of the positive charge of an atom are concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus.
neutrons are present in equal numbers to protons in stable nuclei.
explanation: Most alpha particles passed straight through, but a few were deflected sharply or bounced back. That means the positive charge and most of the mass sit in a very small nucleus. Fixed energy levels belong to Bohr’s model, and the uniform sphere is Thomson’s.

stem: Which pair represents isotopes of the same element?
explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers. Both Pb nuclides have Z = 82. The other pairs share a mass number but are different elements.

stem: An element X forms an oxide XO<sub>3</sub> that contains 48.00% oxygen by mass. Identify X.
explanation: Oxygen in XO<sub>3</sub> has a mass of 3 × 16.00 = 48.00 g per mole, so 48.00% O means the molar mass is 100.0 g/mol and X = 52.0 g/mol, which is chromium (CrO<sub>3</sub>). The source printed 30.06% O, which matches no element in the choices, so it was corrected to 48.00%.

stem: Which species is isoelectronic with the argon atom?
explanation: Argon has 18 electrons. S<sup>2−</sup> has 16 + 2 = 18. Na<sup>+</sup> has 10, Br<sup>−</sup> has 36 and Fe<sup>2+</sup> has 24.

stem: An unknown element M has three isotopes: M-24 (23.9850 amu, 78.99%), M-25 (24.9858 amu, 10.00%) and M-26 (25.9826 amu, 11.01%). What is its atomic weight, and what is the element?
How many electrons are in one nitrate ion (NO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup>)?
explanation: N has 7 electrons and each O has 8, so the three oxygens add 24, giving 31 for the neutral group. The 1− charge adds one more: 32.

stem: What is the correct name of Fe<sub>2</sub>(SO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>·9H<sub>2</sub>O?
explanation: Three sulfate ions (3 × 2−) balance two iron ions, so each iron is 3+, written Iron(III). The nine water molecules in the crystal take the prefix nona-, giving nonahydrate.

stem: What is the formula of perchloric acid?
explanation: The prefix “per-” with “-ic” marks the oxoacid with the most oxygen atoms. The series is hypochlorous HClO, chlorous HClO<sub>2</sub>, chloric HClO<sub>3</sub> and perchloric HClO<sub>4</sub>.

stem: What is the systematic name of the covalent compound P<sub>4</sub>O<sub>10</sub>?
explanation: Covalent binary compounds use Greek prefixes: tetra- for 4 P and deca- for 10 O, with the final “a” dropped before oxide. Mono- is omitted only when the first element has a single atom, which is not the case here.

stem: Which formula is INCORRECT based on standard ionic charges?
explanation: Ba is 2+ and hydrogen carbonate is 1−, so two HCO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup> are needed: Ba(HCO<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>. The other three formulas are charge-balanced.

stem: What is the formula of dinitrogen pentoxide?
explanation: Di- means 2 nitrogen atoms and penta- means 5 oxygen atoms: N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>5</sub>.

stem: What is the name of Cr(BrO<sub>3</sub>)<sub>3</sub>?
explanation: BrO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup> is bromate (bromide is Br<sup>−</sup> and perbromate is BrO<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup>). Three 1− ions mean chromium is 3+, so the name is chromium(III) bromate.

stem: Which oxoacid has a name ending in “-ous acid”?
explanation: “-ous” acids come from “-ite” anions. H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>3</sub> comes from sulfite (SO<sub>3</sub><sup>2−</sup>), so it is sulfurous acid. The others are nitric, phosphoric and perchloric acid, from “-ate” anions.

stem: What is the formula of propane?
explanation: Propane is the 3-carbon alkane. Alkanes follow C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub>, so n = 3 gives C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub>. C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>6</sub> is propene.

stem: What is the formula of ammonium dichromate?
explanation: Ammonium is NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> and dichromate is Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub><sup>2−</sup>, so two ammonium ions balance the 2− charge. The first option is ammonium chromate.

stem: Name the organic compound with the formula CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH.
explanation: A two-carbon chain with an –OH group is ethanol. Methanol has one carbon and propanol has three. Dimethyl ether (CH<sub>3</sub>OCH<sub>3</sub>) is an isomer with no OH group.

stem: How many oxygen atoms are in 0.250 mol of hydrated copper(II) sulfate, CuSO<sub>4</sub>·5H<sub>2</sub>O?
explanation: Each formula unit has 4 O from sulfate plus 5 O from water, so 9 O. Atoms = 0.250 × 9 × 6.022 × 10<sup>23</sup> = 1.35 × 10<sup>24</sup>.

stem: A compound is 40.00% C, 6.71% H and 53.29% O by mass, with a molar mass of about 180 g/mol. What is its molecular formula?
explanation: Per 100 g: C 3.33 mol, H 6.66 mol, O 3.33 mol, so the empirical formula is CH<sub>2</sub>O (30.03 g/mol). 180 ÷ 30.03 = 6, so the molecular formula is C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>.

stem: Burning 1.50 g of a hydrocarbon gives 4.71 g of CO<sub>2</sub> and 1.93 g of H<sub>2</sub>O. What is its empirical formula?
explanation: mol C = 4.71 ÷ 44.01 = 0.1070. mol H = 2 × (1.93 ÷ 18.02) = 0.2142. The ratio H : C is 2.00, so the formula is CH<sub>2</sub>.

stem: What is the mass percent of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate, NH<sub>4</sub>NO<sub>3</sub> (M = 80.04 g/mol)?
explanation: There are two N atoms per formula unit: 2 × 14.01 = 28.02 g. Then 28.02 ÷ 80.04 × 100 = 35.0%.

stem: How many grams of iron can be extracted from 500.0 g of iron(III) oxide, Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> (M = 159.7 g/mol)?
explanation: mol Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> = 500.0 ÷ 159.7 = 3.131. Each gives 2 Fe, so 6.262 mol Fe × 55.85 g/mol = 349.7 g.

stem: A 5.75 g sample of hydrated zinc sulfate, ZnSO<sub>4</sub>·xH<sub>2</sub>O, is heated until all the water is driven off. The anhydrous residue weighs 3.23 g. Find x. (M of ZnSO<sub>4</sub> = 161.47 g/mol; M of H<sub>2</sub>O = 18.02 g/mol)
In a mass spectrometer, xenon is ionized to Xe<sup>+</sup> ions. What determines how far these ions are deflected in the magnetic field?
explanation: In a magnetic field the radius of an ion’s path depends on its m/z: lighter ions, or ions with more charge, bend more. This is how the isotopes of Xe are separated.

stem: How many moles of sodium ions are in a sample containing 3.01 × 10<sup>23</sup> formula units of sodium phosphate, Na<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>?
explanation: 3.01 × 10<sup>23</sup> formula units is 0.500 mol of Na<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub>. Each has 3 Na<sup>+</sup>, so 0.500 × 3 = 1.50 mol.

stem: An oxide of nitrogen contains 30.45% nitrogen by mass. What is its empirical formula?
explanation: Per 100 g: N = 30.45 ÷ 14.01 = 2.173 mol and O = 69.55 ÷ 16.00 = 4.347 mol. The ratio O : N is 2.00, so the formula is NO<sub>2</sub>.

stem: A 2.000 g mixture of NaCl (M = 58.44 g/mol) and KCl (M = 74.55 g/mol) contains 0.0300 mol of chloride ions in total. What is the mass of NaCl in the mixture?
explanation: Let x = mass of NaCl, so KCl = 2.000 − x. Chloride: x/58.44 + (2.000 − x)/74.55 = 0.0300. This gives x ≈ 0.858 g. The closest listed value, and the only one consistent with 0.0300 mol to three figures, is 0.868 g. (The source key listed 0.832 g, which gives 0.0299 mol.)

stem: Consider 2Al(s) + 3Cl<sub>2</sub>(g) → 2AlCl<sub>3</sub>(s). If 10.0 g of Al (M = 26.98 g/mol) reacts with 35.0 g of Cl<sub>2</sub> (M = 70.90 g/mol), what mass of AlCl<sub>3</sub> (M = 133.34 g/mol) forms?
explanation: mol Al = 0.3706 and mol Cl<sub>2</sub> = 0.4937. Al would need 1.5 × 0.3706 = 0.556 mol Cl<sub>2</sub>, so Cl<sub>2</sub> is limiting. AlCl<sub>3</sub> = 0.4937 × (2/3) = 0.3291 mol × 133.34 = 43.9 g. (The source key listed 29.3 g, which does not follow from the data; 49.4 g is what you would get if Al were limiting.)

stem: In the reaction 2Al(s) + 3Cl<sub>2</sub>(g) → 2AlCl<sub>3</sub>(s), 10.0 g of Al (M = 26.98 g/mol) reacts with 35.0 g of Cl<sub>2</sub> (M = 70.90 g/mol). Which reactant is limiting, and how much of the other remains?
choices: Al is limiting; 1.11 g of Cl<sub>2</sub> remains.
Cl<sub>2</sub> is limiting; 1.11 g of Al remains.
Cl<sub>2</sub> is limiting; 5.56 g of Al remains.
Al is limiting; 8.32 g of Cl<sub>2</sub> remains.
explanation: Cl<sub>2</sub> is limiting (0.4937 mol, against the 0.556 mol needed to consume all the Al). It reacts with (2/3) × 0.4937 = 0.3291 mol Al = 8.88 g, leaving 10.0 − 8.88 ≈ 1.1 g of Al.

stem: TiCl<sub>4</sub>(g) + 2Mg(l) → Ti(s) + 2MgCl<sub>2</sub>(l). Reacting 3.54 × 10<sup>7</sup> g of TiCl<sub>4</sub> (M = 189.7 g/mol) with 1.13 × 10<sup>7</sup> g of Mg (M = 24.31 g/mol) gives 7.81 × 10<sup>6</sup> g of Ti (M = 47.87 g/mol). What is the percent yield of Ti?
explanation: mol TiCl<sub>4</sub> = 1.866 × 10<sup>5</sup>; mol Mg = 4.65 × 10<sup>5</sup>, which supports only 2.32 × 10<sup>5</sup> mol Ti, so TiCl<sub>4</sub> is limiting. Theoretical Ti = 1.866 × 10<sup>5</sup> × 47.87 = 8.93 × 10<sup>6</sup> g. Yield = 7.81 × 10<sup>6</sup> ÷ 8.93 × 10<sup>6</sup> = 87.4%.

stem: Balance a C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub>(g) + b O<sub>2</sub>(g) → c CO<sub>2</sub>(g) + d H<sub>2</sub>O(g) with the lowest whole-number coefficients. What is b?
explanation: The balanced equation is 2C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub> + 13O<sub>2</sub> → 8CO<sub>2</sub> + 10H<sub>2</sub>O. Each C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub> needs 4 + 5/2 = 6.5 O<sub>2</sub>; doubling to clear the fraction gives a = 2 and b = 13.

stem: CaC<sub>2</sub>(s) + 2H<sub>2</sub>O(l) → Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub>(s) + C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub>(g). How many grams of acetylene form from 100.0 g of CaC<sub>2</sub> that is 85.0% pure, with excess water? (M of CaC<sub>2</sub> = 64.10 g/mol; M of C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub> = 26.04 g/mol)
explanation: Pure CaC<sub>2</sub> = 0.850 × 100.0 = 85.0 g = 1.326 mol. The ratio is 1 : 1, so C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub> = 1.326 mol × 26.04 = 34.5 g. (40.6 g would ignore the purity.)

stem: N<sub>2</sub>(g) + 3H<sub>2</sub>(g) → 2NH<sub>3</sub>(g). A mixture of 28.0 g N<sub>2</sub> and 9.00 g H<sub>2</sub> produces 25.5 g of NH<sub>3</sub>. What is the percent yield? (M of N<sub>2</sub> = 28.02, H<sub>2</sub> = 2.016, NH<sub>3</sub> = 17.03 g/mol)
explanation: mol N<sub>2</sub> = 0.9993 and mol H<sub>2</sub> = 4.464 (only 3 × 0.9993 = 2.998 is needed), so N<sub>2</sub> is limiting. Theoretical NH<sub>3</sub> = 2 × 0.9993 = 1.999 mol = 34.04 g. Yield = 25.5 ÷ 34.04 = 74.9%, about 75.0%. (The source key listed 85.0%, which does not follow from the data.)

stem: Sulfuric acid is made in three steps: S<sub>8</sub> + 8O<sub>2</sub> → 8SO<sub>2</sub>; 2SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2SO<sub>3</sub>; SO<sub>3</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O → H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>. Starting from 1.00 kg of sulfur (S<sub>8</sub>, M = 256.5 g/mol), what is the maximum mass of H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> (M = 98.08 g/mol) with a quantitative yield in every step?
explanation: One S<sub>8</sub> gives 8 SO<sub>2</sub>, then 8 SO<sub>3</sub>, then 8 H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>. mol S<sub>8</sub> = 1000 ÷ 256.5 = 3.899, so H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> = 31.19 mol × 98.08 = 3059 g = 3.06 kg.

stem: 2.00 mol of H<sub>2</sub> and 2.00 mol of O<sub>2</sub> are ignited: 2H<sub>2</sub>(g) + O<sub>2</sub>(g) → 2H<sub>2</sub>O(g). How many total moles of gas are in the container after the reaction is complete?
explanation: H<sub>2</sub> is limiting: 2.00 mol H<sub>2</sub> uses 1.00 mol O<sub>2</sub> and makes 2.00 mol H<sub>2</sub>O(g). Remaining gas = 1.00 mol O<sub>2</sub> + 2.00 mol H<sub>2</sub>O = 3.00 mol. (The source key listed 2.50 mol, which does not follow.)

stem: When 0.500 mol of a metal M reacts completely with excess nitrogen gas, 0.167 mol of a nitride M<sub>x</sub>N<sub>y</sub> forms. What is x?
explanation: All 0.500 mol of M ends up in the product, so x = 0.500 ÷ 0.167 = 3, as in a nitride such as Mg<sub>3</sub>N<sub>2</sub>.

stem: Aspirin is made from salicylic acid (C<sub>7</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O<sub>3</sub>, M = 138.12 g/mol) and acetic anhydride (C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O<sub>3</sub>, M = 102.09 g/mol): C<sub>7</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O<sub>3</sub> → C<sub>9</sub>H<sub>8</sub>O<sub>4</sub> + C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O<sub>2</sub> (aspirin, M = 180.16 g/mol). If 2.00 g of each reactant is used and the yield is 85.0%, what mass of aspirin is collected?
explanation: mol salicylic acid = 0.01448 and mol anhydride = 0.01959 (a 1 : 1 reaction), so salicylic acid is limiting. Theoretical aspirin = 0.01448 × 180.16 = 2.609 g. At 85.0%: 2.609 × 0.850 = 2.22 g.

topic: Chemistry: A Science for the Twenty-First Century
stem: Chemistry is often called the central science because it…
choices: links physics and mathematics with biology, geology and medicine
explanation: Chemistry explains the matter and changes that underlie physics, biology, earth science and medicine.

topic: Chemistry: A Science for the Twenty-First Century
stem: Which process is used to make fertilizer from nitrogen in the air?
explanation: The Haber process combines N<sub>2</sub> and H<sub>2</sub> to make ammonia, the basis of most fertilizers.

topic: Chemistry: A Science for the Twenty-First Century
stem: Which statement about chemistry is correct?
choices: It studies matter, its properties and the changes it undergoes.
It has no link to environmental issues.
It cannot be used to make predictions.
explanation: Chemistry covers all matter and its changes, natural or man-made, and it makes testable predictions.

topic: Chemistry: A Science for the Twenty-First Century
stem: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) were phased out mainly because they…
explanation: CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere, which destroy ozone.

topic: Chemistry: A Science for the Twenty-First Century
stem: Which is a goal of green chemistry?
choices: Designing processes that reduce hazardous waste
Making reactions as fast as possible regardless of cost
explanation: Green chemistry aims to prevent waste and to use safer substances and processes.

stem: In chemistry, the macroscopic level refers to…
choices: what can be observed and measured directly
only the nucleus of an atom
explanation: Colour, mass, temperature and volume are macroscopic; atoms and molecules are the microscopic explanation.

stem: Which is a macroscopic observation?
choices: A bond breaks in a molecule.
explanation: A colour change can be seen directly. The other options describe particles.

stem: Explaining why ice floats by describing how water molecules are arranged is an explanation at the…
explanation: It uses molecules and their arrangement to explain an observed property.

stem: “Mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction” is the law of…
explanation: The total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.

stem: In chemistry, a substance is…
choices: matter with a fixed composition and distinct properties
explanation: Elements and compounds are substances; mixtures are not, because their composition varies.

stem: A tentative explanation that can be tested by experiment is a…
explanation: A hypothesis is testable and may be revised or rejected.

stem: A concise statement of a consistent pattern in many observations, without explaining why, is a…
explanation: A law describes what happens; a theory explains why.

stem: A well-tested explanation that accounts for a wide range of observations is a…
explanation: Theories such as atomic theory are supported by large amounts of evidence.

stem: In a controlled experiment, the quantity the experimenter deliberately changes is the…
explanation: The independent variable is changed, the dependent variable is measured, and everything else is held constant.

stem: Experimental results contradict a hypothesis. The correct scientific response is to…
explanation: Hypotheses must agree with the evidence; the data decide.

stem: Which is a pure substance?
explanation: Distilled water is a single compound, H<sub>2</sub>O. Air, seawater and brass are mixtures.

stem: Which is a heterogeneous mixture?
explanation: Granite has visibly different regions. The others are uniform (homogeneous).

stem: Which is a compound?
explanation: A compound contains two or more elements in a fixed ratio. The others are elements.

stem: Which method separates sugar from a sugar–water solution?
explanation: Sugar is dissolved, so filtering does not work. Evaporating the water leaves the sugar behind.

stem: Which state of matter has a definite volume but no definite shape?
explanation: A liquid keeps its volume but takes the shape of its container.

stem: Which statement about gases is correct?
choices: The particles are far apart and move freely.
The particles are held in fixed positions.
explanation: Gas particles have large spaces between them, so gases fill their container and compress easily.

stem: The change from gas directly to solid is called…
explanation: Sublimation is solid to gas; deposition is the reverse.

stem: Which phase change absorbs heat (is endothermic)?
explanation: Melting needs energy to loosen the particles; the others release energy.

stem: Solids are very hard to compress because…
choices: their particles are already in contact
there are no attractions between particles
explanation: There is almost no empty space between the particles to squeeze out.

topic: Physical and Chemical Properties of Matter
stem: Which is a chemical property?
explanation: Flammability describes how a substance reacts with oxygen. The others can be measured without changing the substance.

topic: Physical and Chemical Properties of Matter
stem: Which is a physical change?
explanation: Boiling changes the state only; the molecules stay H<sub>2</sub>O.

topic: Physical and Chemical Properties of Matter
stem: Which is an extensive property?
explanation: Mass depends on the amount of sample; density, temperature and boiling point do not.

stem: What is the SI base unit of mass?
explanation: The kilogram is the SI base unit; the gram is a fraction of it.

stem: What is 5.0 × 10<sup>3</sup> mg in grams?
explanation: 1 mg = 10<sup>−3</sup> g, so 5.0 × 10<sup>3</sup> mg = 5.0 g.

stem: Convert 25 °C to kelvin.
Express 0.000 045 6 in scientific notation.
explanation: Move the decimal 5 places to the right to get 4.56, so the exponent is −5.

stem: Calculate (3.20 × 10<sup>3</sup>)(2.0 × 10<sup>−2</sup>) with the correct significant figures.
explanation: The product is 64. The factor 2.0 has two significant figures, so the answer has two.

stem: Round 2.7451 to three significant figures.
explanation: The digits after 2.74 are 51, which is more than half, so round up to 2.75.

stem: Convert 72.0 km/h to m/s.
A car travels 150 km on 12.0 L of fuel. What is its consumption in L per 100 km?
How many seconds are in 2.50 hours?
According to Dalton’s atomic theory, all atoms of a given element…
choices: are identical in mass and properties
explanation: Dalton proposed that atoms of the same element are alike and differ from atoms of other elements.

stem: Dalton’s idea that compounds contain atoms in fixed whole-number ratios explains the law of…
explanation: A compound always has the same elements in the same mass ratio.

stem: Two compounds of carbon and oxygen contain 1.33 g and 2.67 g of oxygen per 1.00 g of carbon. This illustrates the law of…
explanation: The oxygen masses are in a simple ratio, 1 : 2. That is the law of multiple proportions.

stem: In a chemical reaction, atoms are…
choices: rearranged but not created or destroyed
explanation: Bonds break and form, but each atom survives, so mass is conserved.

stem: Which part of Dalton’s theory was later shown to be incorrect?
explanation: Atoms contain protons, neutrons and electrons, so they can be divided.

stem: Which subatomic particle has no charge and a mass close to that of a proton?
explanation: Neutrons are neutral with a mass of about 1 amu.

stem: Most alpha particles passed straight through Rutherford’s gold foil. This showed that atoms are…
explanation: Only a tiny nucleus could deflect the particles, so most of the atom is empty space.

stem: Thomson’s cathode-ray experiments showed that cathode rays are…
explanation: The rays were deflected by electric and magnetic fields, so they are negatively charged particles: electrons.

topic: Atomic Number, Mass Number, and Isotopes
stem: The atomic number of an element is the number of…
explanation: Z counts protons and defines the element.

stem: Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties because they have the same number of…
explanation: Valence electrons control bonding and reactions.

stem: Which is an alkali metal?
explanation: The alkali metals are Group 1: Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs and Fr.

stem: Which group contains the halogens?
explanation: F, Cl, Br, I and At are in Group 17.

stem: Which element is a metalloid?
explanation: Silicon sits on the metal/nonmetal boundary. Al is a metal; C and S are nonmetals.

stem: Which pair of elements has the most similar chemical properties?
explanation: Cl and Br are in the same group (the halogens).

stem: Which is a diatomic molecule of an element?
explanation: N<sub>2</sub> has two atoms of the same element. CO and H<sub>2</sub>O are compounds, and NaCl is ionic.

stem: An atom that loses electrons forms a…
explanation: Losing negative electrons leaves a positive ion, a cation.

stem: How many protons and electrons are in Mg<sup>2+</sup>? (Mg: Z = 12)
explanation: Protons stay at 12; a 2+ ion has lost two electrons, leaving 10.

stem: What is the empirical formula of hydrogen peroxide, H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>?
explanation: Divide the subscripts by their common factor, 2.

stem: How many atoms are in one formula unit of Ca(NO<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>?
explanation: 1 Ca + 2 N + 6 O = 9 atoms. The subscript 2 multiplies everything inside the brackets.

stem: What is the name of FeCl<sub>2</sub>?
explanation: Two Cl<sup>−</sup> ions mean Fe is 2+, so the name is iron(II) chloride.

topic: Chemistry: A Science for the Twenty-First Century
stem: Which is an everyday example of chemistry?
explanation: Cooking changes the proteins in the egg into new forms, a chemical change. The others are physics.

topic: Chemistry: A Science for the Twenty-First Century
stem: Which achievement is mainly chemistry?
explanation: Making new substances from other substances is chemistry.

topic: Chemistry: A Science for the Twenty-First Century
stem: Why can chemistry help with problems such as climate change?
choices: It explains how substances like CO<sub>2</sub> react, absorb energy and can be captured or converted
It can change the laws of physics
It can stop all reactions in the atmosphere
explanation: Knowing how gases and materials react lets chemists design cleaner fuels, catalysts and capture methods.

stem: Water boiling is explained at the particle level by…
choices: molecules gaining enough energy to separate from one another
oxygen atoms turning into hydrogen atoms
explanation: Boiling is a physical change: the H<sub>2</sub>O molecules stay intact but move apart.

stem: Which of these is matter?
explanation: Matter has mass and takes up space. Air is made of gas particles; heat, light and sound are not matter.

stem: A sealed flask has the same mass before and after an iron nail rusts inside it. This is consistent with…
choices: a change in the number of atoms
explanation: In a closed system atoms are only rearranged, so the total mass stays the same.

stem: Which is a quantitative observation?
choices: The solution has a mass of 25.3 g.
explanation: Quantitative observations are numerical measurements; the others are qualitative.

stem: To test a fertilizer, one group of plants gets it and another group does not, with identical soil, light and water. The group without fertilizer is the…
explanation: The control is treated the same way except for the factor being tested.

stem: Why is it important to repeat an experiment?
choices: It shows whether the result is reproducible
It removes the need for data
It turns a hypothesis into a law
explanation: Reproducible results give confidence that the outcome is not due to chance or error.

stem: Which is a homogeneous mixture?
explanation: A solution is uniform throughout. The others have visibly separate parts.

stem: Which is an element?
explanation: S<sub>8</sub> contains only sulfur atoms. The others are compounds.

stem: Which statement about elements and compounds is correct?
choices: A compound can be broken down by chemical reactions; an element cannot.
An element can be separated by filtration.
A compound is always a mixture.
An element contains more than one kind of atom.
explanation: Compounds have two or more elements chemically bonded and can be decomposed chemically; elements cannot be broken down by chemical means.

stem: In which state are the particles close together but able to slide past each other?
explanation: Liquid particles touch but are not fixed in position.

stem: Dry ice (solid CO<sub>2</sub>) turns directly into gas at atmospheric pressure. This change is called…
explanation: Solid to gas without a liquid stage is sublimation.

stem: Which change releases heat to the surroundings?
explanation: Condensation releases energy as particles come together. The other three absorb energy.

topic: Physical and Chemical Properties of Matter
stem: Which is a physical property?
explanation: Boiling point can be measured without changing the substance. The others describe reactions.

topic: Physical and Chemical Properties of Matter
stem: Which observation indicates a chemical change?
choices: Gas bubbles form and a new solid appears when two clear solutions are mixed
A solid is crushed into powder
explanation: New substances (a gas and a solid) have formed. The other changes are physical.

topic: Physical and Chemical Properties of Matter
stem: Which property is intensive?
explanation: Density is the same for any amount of the substance.

stem: A liquid has a density of 0.789 g/mL. What is the mass of 250.0 mL?
What is 0.0045 km in metres?
Using °F = 1.8 °C + 32, what is 100 °C in °F?
explanation: 1.8 × 100 + 32 = 212 °F, the boiling point of water.

stem: How many significant figures are in 0.0502?
explanation: Leading zeros do not count; 5, 0 and 2 do.

stem: What is 12.11 + 18.0 + 1.013 to the correct number of decimal places?
explanation: The sum is 31.123. The least precise value, 18.0, has one decimal place, so the answer is 31.1.

stem: Write 6.02 × 10<sup>5</sup> in ordinary notation.
explanation: A positive exponent of 5 moves the decimal five places to the right.

stem: How many cm<sup>3</sup> are in 2.5 L?
explanation: 1 L = 1000 cm<sup>3</sup>, so 2.5 L = 2500 cm<sup>3</sup>.

stem: Convert 15.0 m<sup>3</sup> to litres.
Gold has a density of 19.3 g/cm<sup>3</sup>. What is the mass in kg of a 5.00 cm × 4.00 cm × 2.00 cm gold bar?
Who proposed the modern atomic theory in 1808?
explanation: Dalton’s atomic theory explained the laws of chemical combination.

stem: Water always has a hydrogen-to-oxygen mass ratio of about 1 : 8. Which law does this support?
explanation: A given compound always has the same elements in the same mass ratio.

stem: Carbon forms CO and CO<sub>2</sub>. For the same mass of carbon, what is the ratio of oxygen masses in CO<sub>2</sub> to CO?
explanation: CO<sub>2</sub> has twice as many O atoms per C atom as CO. Small whole-number ratios illustrate multiple proportions.

stem: Which particle is found outside the nucleus?
explanation: Electrons surround the nucleus; protons and neutrons are inside it.

stem: A proton is roughly how many times heavier than an electron?
explanation: The proton mass (1.67 × 10<sup>−24</sup> g) is about 1840 times the electron mass.

stem: In Rutherford’s experiment a few alpha particles were deflected at large angles because they…
choices: hit the small, dense, positively charged nucleus
explanation: Large deflections need a concentrated positive charge to repel the positive alpha particles.

topic: Atomic Number, Mass Number, and Isotopes
stem: How many neutrons are in <sup>238</sup>U? (Z = 92)
explanation: Neutrons = A − Z = 238 − 92 = 146.

topic: Atomic Number, Mass Number, and Isotopes
stem: Which pair are isotopes of the same element?
explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number (here 6) but different mass numbers.

topic: Atomic Number, Mass Number, and Isotopes
stem: Copper has two isotopes, <sup>63</sup>Cu (62.93 amu, 69.15%) and <sup>65</sup>Cu (64.93 amu). What is the average atomic mass?
Which of these is a noble gas?
explanation: Argon is in Group 18.

stem: Which statement is true of metals compared with nonmetals?
choices: Metals tend to lose electrons and conduct electricity well.
explanation: Metals lose electrons to form cations and are good conductors.

stem: How many elements are in Period 2?
explanation: Period 2 runs from Li (Z = 3) to Ne (Z = 10): eight elements.

stem: What is the charge on the sulfide ion formed from sulfur (Group 16)?
explanation: Group 16 atoms gain 2 electrons to reach a noble-gas configuration.

stem: Which is a polyatomic cation?
explanation: Ammonium is a group of atoms carrying a positive charge. The others are anions.

stem: How many electrons are in the chloride ion, Cl<sup>−</sup>? (Cl: Z = 17)
explanation: Neutral Cl has 17 electrons; gaining one gives 18.

stem: What is the empirical formula of glucose, C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>?
explanation: Divide every subscript by 6.

stem: What is the formula of the compound formed by Mg<sup>2+</sup> and PO<sub>4</sub><sup>3−</sup>?
explanation: Three Mg<sup>2+</sup> (6+) balance two PO<sub>4</sub><sup>3−</sup> (6−).

stem: Which kind of formula shows how the atoms in a molecule are connected?
explanation: A structural formula draws the bonds between atoms.

stem: What is the formula of sodium sulfite?
explanation: Sulfite is SO<sub>3</sub><sup>2−</sup>; sulfate is SO<sub>4</sub><sup>2−</sup>. Two Na<sup>+</sup> balance one 2− ion.

stem: What is the name of CO?
explanation: The first element takes no mono- prefix; the second takes mono-, written “monoxide”.

stem: What is the name of HBr dissolved in water?
explanation: Binary acids are named hydro-…-ic acid.
